title: Controlling in Management Explained | Principles of Management Ep 19
description:
How does a manager know if a plan is really working? In this animated lesson, Ravi's second Chai Corner outlet has been open for a month. The plan was 500 cups a day, but some cups are half empty, some customers wait five minutes, and nobody has counted the cups even once.

You will learn what controlling means (checking that actual performance matches the plan, and fixing it when it doesn't), the 5 steps of the control process (set standards, measure actual performance, compare with the standard, analyse the deviation, take corrective action), why controlling is a feedback loop, why planning and controlling are called the Siamese twins of management, and management by exception, which Frederick Taylor called the exception principle.

This is Episode 19 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.

In this video:
0:00 A plan nobody checks
0:23 What is controlling?
0:36 The 5 steps of controlling
1:20 The feedback loop
1:28 Planning and controlling: the Siamese twins
1:44 Management by exception
2:03 Quick check
2:17 Recap

Next episode: Management by Objectives (MBO).
